title: The Value of a Chance: Task Concentration and Talent Discovery in Team Production
abstract: arXiv:2511.07218v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Organizations often concentrate scarce, high-value tasks on proven performers, but doing so may limit opportunities to develop and learn about alternative workers. We study this trade-off using temporary injuries to high-performing Major League Baseball players, which generate plausibly exogenous reallocations of playing opportunities. Tracking allocation and performance before, during, and after these absences, we find clear evidence of crowd-out: when a high performer becomes unavailable, same-team, same-position coworkers receive substantially more opportunities. Yet we find little evidence that the additional experience raises batting productivity during the absence or after the high performer returns, suggesting that learning by doing is not the main dynamic benefit. translated_title: 机会的价值：团队生产中的任务集中与人才发现
translated_abstract: 组织常常将稀缺且高价值的任务集中在已被证明的绩效者身上，但这可能会限制其他员工的发展和学习机会。我们利用美国职业棒球大联盟中高绩效球员的临时伤病来研究这一权衡，这些伤病导致了看似外生的比赛机会重新分配。通过追踪这些缺阵期间、期间和之后的机会分配与表现，我们发现了明显的挤出效应：当高绩效球员无法上场时，同队同位置的队友获得了显著更多的机会。然而，我们几乎没有发现额外经验在缺阵期间或高绩效球员回归后能提高击球生产力的证据，这表明“干中学”并非主要的动态收益。相反，缺阵期间的表现惊喜能预测后续的就业和比赛机会，这与团队利用新揭示的信息进行决策的假设一致。
tldr: 本研究通过棒球球员伤病数据发现，任务集中虽挤出替代者的机会，但额外经验并未提升生产力，而表现惊喜揭示的信息才是人才发现和后续机会分配的关键。
en_tdlr: This study, using baseball player injury data, finds that task concentration crowds out substitutes' opportunities, yet additional experience does not boost productivity; instead, performance surprises reveal information crucial for talent discovery and subsequent opportunity allocation.
